content.thinking:
I'm planning the chest's proportions—roughly 0.9m wide body with an open lid, scaling the whole scene to about 1.4m wide including a coin pile. I'm mapping out which geometry primitives to use for the model (lathe, extrude, sweep, rod) and setting up a root joint for the structure.

For the lid, I'm designing it with a hinge joint and working out how to position it open by defining points in lid-local space, then transforming them into model space with a rotation around the hinge axis—building a helper function that combines the hinge rotation with each part's local orientation.

I'm thinking through the lid's shape itself, considering a half-cylinder barrel form versus simple box slabs, and weighing how the interior should render when the lid is open since viewers would see its underside—settling toward building it from flat box panels for simplicity.

Still shaping the lid geometry...

Now I'm working out the hinge rotation: the lid swings about the X axis from closed (local +z pointing forward) to an open angle past vertical (~105°), with the hinge positioned at the back edge, so I'm deriving the rotation matrix for angle θ that maps local +z to the appropriate world direction as it swings up and back.

I settle on θ=100° so the lid leans back slightly, exposing its underside toward the viewer like the reference image shows. Then I'm sizing the box body itself, spanning roughly 0.9 wide by 0.5 deep by 0.42 tall, sitting just above the floor on the coin pile.

For decoration, I plan a flattened mound shape on top of the body to suggest heaped coins, plus scattered coin shapes. I'm also thinking through how to texture the wooden box using a cel-shaded blue paint with a wood-grain pattern layered underneath for the painted panels.

Now I'm working out gold paint variation for the coins using mottled shading, and considering gem shapes—using faceted low-poly geometry with flat shading and a soft glow, in red, blue, green, and purple to suggest jewels.

I'll dial glow strength down to 0.4 so emissive color adds to lit faces without washing out faceting. For coins, I'm planning to reuse a small cylinder geometry merged across instances to stay within the part budget, and thinking about whether to add a gold texture with a fleur emblem using the cylinder's default cap UV mapping.

I'll draw a full-square gold background with a darker rim ring and fleur emblem so the side view just shows muted gold banding from the squashed texture, which should look acceptable even if messy. For merging, I'll keep all cylinder geometries with identical attributes so mergeGeometries works cleanly, applying each coin's transform matrix before combining, with the texture map carrying the actual colors rather than vertex colors or cel-shading.

For variety I'll make two gold textures, one brighter and one slightly darker, and merge coins using each to create tonal variation across the pile. I'm scattering coins in rings around the chest base with randomized height and tilt, plus building coin stacks from repeated cylinder geometry with jitter offsets—estimating roughly 48 triangles per 12-segment coin, so around 400 coins lands near 19k triangles total.

I'll scale down to 10 radial segments (40 tris each) and target about 450 coins to stay under 60k total triangles, using a deterministic RNG for coin placement to avoid messy overlaps. For layout, I'm centering the chest at origin and building a flattened ellipsoid "mound" shape under the pile to give coins a natural heap slope, computing each coin's height on the mound surface with an ellipse equation and adding small random tilts, while coins beyond the mound's radius sit flat on the floor.

To avoid the mound sinking visibly below the floor, I'll switch to a half-sphere geometry (open bottom, hidden anyway) rather than a full sphere. The chest body sits with its base partially embedded in the mound like the reference image, built from separate front/back/side/bottom panel boxes with a gold rim, and the interior coin mound is scaled and positioned near the top opening so coins can be placed across its surface using the same ellipse height function.

For the interior, I'll add a thin red lining box in front of the back panel to simulate the inner red fabric, since the mound hides the rest of the interior. For the gold trim, I'm adding corner posts and rim boxes along the top and bottom edges of the body to frame it.

For decoration, I'm designing a lion-head ring knocker using a torus plus a gold diamond plaque, with the lion face built from a scaled sphere, cone-ring mane spikes, a small muzzle box, and dark eye gems, wrapped into a reusable lionHead helper function. I'm also planning gold fleur-de-lis decals as textured planes placed slightly offset from the blue panels on either side of the plaque.

Now I'm planning side ring handles with torus rings rotated to face outward on the left and right, paired with gold backplates, and working out the lid's cross-section profile with gold end caps and middle ribs positioned along the outline.

I'm also adding a center diamond gold plate with a blue gem on the lid top, plus expanded gold bands, and planning the underside red lining for when the lid is open...

Still writing geometry...

Working out the slope panel geometry, computing lengths and angles for the diagonal pieces, then figuring out the local rotation quaternions needed to orient each box segment correctly.

Writing panel helper code...

Then I'm figuring out the gold rim frame around the opening's perimeter underneath, positioning boxes along each edge to form the lip.

Now I'm working out the diamond-shaped gold plate embedded in the lid's top surface, needing to extrude it along the correct axis to match the lid's orientation.

I'm placing a central gem on the plate with smaller corner gems, then adding rivets as merged sphere clusters along the end caps and planning hinge barrel cylinders for the back of the lid.

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: a root spine joint, then a lid joint parented to root at the hinge position with a hinge role, working out the correct direction and roll for the hinge axis.

Parts attached to the lid bone get placed in model space using their own `at` coordinates. Next I'm positioning the crown on top of the pile inside the chest, roughly center-right and slightly tilted, scaling it relative to the chest's size.

Modeling the crown's band and arches...

Looking at the reference again, I'll simplify to a gold band at the bottom with jewels rather than ermine fur, then add eight fleur-de-lis spikes alternating with pearl tips around the band's top edge.

Still defining the rig class...

Still refining the goblet's cup profile, making sure the outer and inner wall curves close up into a proper hollow shell without the lathe outline crossing itself.

I'm planning decorative details now: a darker gold torus band circling the cup, plus a small emblem or crest texture (like a fleur-de-lis) applied as a decal on the front.

I'll use the decal only on the upright goblet, skipping it for the fallen one since that'll just rely on the rim torus and gems. For the fallen goblet lying tipped over the chest's right front edge, I need to position it pointing right-down with the foot sticking outward at the top-right.

For the orientation, I'm computing an aim quaternion so the goblet's local y-axis points toward the correct direction instead of using setFromUnitVectors directly. Since the cup opening faces left toward the pile and the foot points right, the up-axis direction should be roughly (-0.9, -0.15, -0.3).

Now I'm positioning the goblet's foot and sizing it so the cup extends toward the mound, with a few coins spilling near the mouth. I'm also planning the pearl necklace and gold chain with pendant draped over the front edge, sketching a catmull-rom path that sweeps from the mound surface up over the lip in a hanging catenary curve.

Writing pearl and chain code...

Scaling z gives vertical elongation since forward aim with no up puts +Z as the up direction. Now I'm planning the gem pile layout — roughly a dozen scattered gems of varying sizes (0.1–0.17 wide), with a big red gem near the floor front, a blue one on the mound, plus green and purple accents, each tilted at slightly random upward angles to look naturally strewn.

I'm now working out a height function for the mound shapes so gems sit properly on the surface rather than floating — using an elliptical profile for the floor mound (centered around x=0, z=0.1, with semi-axes roughly 0.9 and 0.65) to compute how high the pile rises at any given x,z position, checking that it reasonably covers the lower portion of the chest front.

Then I'm placing coins and small gems onto that mound with slight random tilts for a natural scattered look, and defining a similar smaller mound inside the chest itself where a crown piece can rest on top, making sure the chest mound stays within the chest's interior wall bounds.

For coin placement I need to exclude circular regions around the crown and goblet so coins don't visually intersect them, while letting gems and necklaces overlap slightly since that looks natural. I'm also scattering a few separate coin stacks around the base of the mound at varied positions, each stack having several coins with small random jitter for realism.

Now I'm figuring out coin dimensions—roughly 0.1m diameter and 0.012m thick—and planning a broader scatter of coins lying flat across the floor around the mound, staying within an elliptical boundary but avoiding the chest's footprint.

I'm also budgeting coin counts across the scene: around 200 on the floor mound, 120 on the chest mound, 60 scattered loosely, and 40 in stacks, totaling roughly 450 coins for the triangle budget.

Each coin uses about 40 triangles (sides plus caps), giving roughly 18k triangles total. I'm figuring out how to merge coin geometries by cloning and transforming each with a composed matrix built from position and an Euler-based quaternion for tilt and yaw, then merging the resulting position, normal, and UV attributes.

For the coin texture, I'm designing an SVG with a golden rim and a fleur-de-lis emblem made of curved petal paths in the center.

Writing SVG code...

Setting up cap UV mapping for the cylinder, then planning a gold fleur decal texture on a transparent background to apply as textured plane panels.

Now I'm positioning fleur decals and lion plaque on the blue front panel, working out their x/y placement relative to center and figuring out z-offsets so the decal sits just above the panel's outer surface without clipping into the corner posts.

I'm also working out the gold trim placement—top and bottom rim boxes sized and centered relative to the body's height range, keeping the panel visually inset from the posts.

For the side mound geometry, I check an ellipse formula at the side position to confirm the height stays small and consistent with the front mound. For the blue panel texture, I'm defining a procedural paint function that creates horizontal plank lines by checking fractional position along y and switching between a dark blue line color and a mottled base fill.

Writing panel paint logic...

For the gold color, I'm wrapping a mottled yellow-orange texture in a cel-shading function, letting it auto-derive shadows from the base color since no explicit shadow or glow is needed for gold surfaces. I also start defining a darker gold variant for contrast.

Now I'm sketching flat color assignments for trim and velvet lining, then moving to the lion head emblem on the front: positioning a hexagonal gold plaque with beveled edges at a specific coordinate, followed by planning the lion's mane as a radial arrangement of cone shapes.

Still building the lion face...

Adding ring hardware on both sides, then placing small pyramid-cone spikes and rivets along the top corners and rim for extra ornamentation.

Now I'm designing the lid: blue painted panels with gold end caps and bands, a diamond plate with a blue gem on top, hinge barrels, and corner spikes mirroring the star ornaments from the reference. For the underside I'm adding a velvet-style lining with a diagonal quilted paint pattern and a gold border trim.

Working out the quilt geometry...

Now I'm figuring out where to place the crown on the mound, computing its height and tilt so it sits naturally in 3/4 view, then starting to lay out the crown's band geometry.

Still writing crown geometry...

Defining arch geometry and orb placement...

I'll offset the fleurs by 22.5° so they sit evenly between the four arch feet, giving eight fleurs alternating with four arches. Then for the band jewels, I'm defining the front gem placement using a radial direction vector based on angle from the +z axis.

Placing jewels around twelve stations—a big oversized red gem at the front, with smaller alternating blue, green, and pearl gems at ±40° and ±80°—oriented so each gem faces outward along its radial direction, with scale adjustments for the oversized red stone. I'm also adding a gold surround beneath the big gem using a flattened sphere shape as a setting.

Writing lathe geometry code...

I'm applying glow to the gems with shared flat-color materials cloned per source. For colors I'm picking ruby, sapphire, emerald, amethyst, maybe topaz, and considering small sparkle star decals as glowing front-facing cards near the larger gems for a League-style highlight effect.

I'll place a handful of these sparkles (small size) near the gems and crown using glowing white-plane textures shaped like four-point stars, offset slightly toward the camera since they're only visible from the front. Now I'm positioning the second goblet on the chest mound, calculating its height offset based on the mound's curve at that x-coordinate.

Then I'm working through the lid geometry when open: tracking the hinge angle to figure out where the lid's top edge and hump land vertically, checking that the total piece height (lid, crown, orb) comes to roughly 1.0 to match the reference proportions. I'm adjusting the lid depth from 0.5 to about 0.52 and reworking the profile coordinates accordingly.

Still placing lid hardware... I'm positioning the hinge, gold end caps, and decorative bands across the lid, sizing a slightly larger outline for the bands and checking whether they'd poke through to the red lining underneath.

Checking the band's top clearance of 0.015 above the panel looks right, and the slope roughly tracks the panel's outer edge, just slightly wider, which should be fine visually.

Looking at the band's bottom surface at y=0.02 — since it sits inside the red block's volume where the block occupies y from 0 upward, that face would be hidden and not visible anyway. The gold lip frame and underside look correct.

Now checking the red block's extrusion dimensions and coordinates for the lid.

Working through where the outline polygon points sit and verifying the underside wall gets painted correctly along the thickness axis.

I'm now adding the chest's interior back lining panel — a thin red box positioned at the back wall.

I'm also setting up matching left and right interior lining panels at the box's inner sides, then placing the bottom floor box for the body underneath. Now I'm thinking about scattering coins on the chest mound and along the rim, including some leaning against the front edge.

Skipping extra ingots and bars in favor of small ruby clusters to keep the palette focused. For the pearl strand, I'm computing where it drapes over the front mound curve, calculating the surface height at a few x-positions to place the string's control points naturally along the pile.

Now I'm checking the pearl path against the rim geometry to make sure it clears the front rim box at z 0.25-0.28, keeping clear of the lion plaque and fleur decorations at x=±0.28. I'm working out a similar hanging chain on the right side with a pendant terminating around x=0.2.

Still writing chain path...

I'm noticing the fleur and pendant positions nearly overlap, so I'll shift the fleurs outward to ±0.33 for clearance. Then I'll keep the overall footprint bounded within roughly ±1.0 in x and up to y~1.0, and scatter coins across the surface while letting gems sit slightly raised above the floor height plus their radius.

Now I'm generating the coin scatter: sampling points in an elliptical mound region using polar coordinates, excluding the chest's footprint area and deciding how much of the hidden back region to still include so coins remain visible from that viewing angle.

I'm also adding slight random tilt and vertical offset per coin so they look naturally scattered on the slope, then placing a second ring of coins in an annulus around the mound to extend onto the flatter floor area outside it.

Tallying it up, I'm aiming for roughly 330 floor coins plus 110 mound coins and 40 stacked ones, landing near 480 coins total and about 19k triangles -- reasonable for performance.

For the mound coins I'm scattering them within an ellipse but excluding zones already occupied by the crown, the standing goblet, and the fallen goblet, so coins don't overlap those props, with slight tilt variation and height following the mound's curve.

Now I'm defining the coin stack positions scattered across the floor, each with a jittered base location and coin count, stacking individual coin meshes upward with small random offsets in position and yaw so they look naturally piled rather than perfectly aligned. I'm also starting to lay out the gem placements on the mound, defining each gem's position, color, size, and tilt direction relative to the floor height.

I'm computing the vertical offset using the sphere surface equation, then placing a large sapphire gem near the crown at roughly (-0.02, 0.16) with radius 0.06.

Checking emerald and ruby placement, I realize they overlap with the crown's footprint, so I need to shift the crown backward in z and move the gems forward slightly to avoid collision, while also accounting for the coin exclusion zone around the crown's base.

I'm defining a height function for the chest surface so gems sit correctly on top, orienting each gem with a tilt direction and adding small glowing sparkle planes near them. I'm also planning fleur decorations on the chest's side panels, positioning them on the outer faces so they're visible from the sides.

Deciding to skip the side fleurs and keep just rings and gold side plates for simplicity, then moving to the mound geometry -- using a mottled gold material for the sphere and a darker gold tone underneath the coins, while making sure the mound base sits flush with the floor at y=0 and the coin thickness is centered correctly above it.

Now I'm working out the fallen goblet's orientation, positioning its foot near the chest's right edge resting on the mound, with the cup axis extending toward the pile. I'm checking whether the mound surface actually extends far enough to support the cup's mouth position, since the normalized distance calculation suggests that point falls outside the mound's radius.

I'll scatter a few spilled coins near the goblet's mouth, then add decorative elements for both the fallen and standing goblets — a rim torus with gems for the fallen one, and a decal with a fleur crest texture applied to the standing goblet's cup surface.

Working out the decal placement relative to the goblet's lathe origin and radius, projecting it onto the cup's front surface. Now I'm setting up a Rig helper class to track position and orientation for positioning these objects consistently.

Still writing helper functions...

Still working through the type handling...

Still writing helper functions...

Defining the rest of the color palette...

Writing plank and fleur SVG code...

Designing the star shape and coin textures now, then moving on to the lion ornament and lid's sapphire star-point extrusion details for the 3D model.

I'm checking the lid's exterior visibility in the reference image—since we mostly see the interior and side edges, exterior detail can stay moderate while still getting the rotation math right for the lid's local axis orientation.

Verifying the hinge geometry places the lid underside facing forward toward the viewer with the hump tilting back, then checking that the lid's swing path clears the crown and goblet without collision as it rises.

Setting up the hinge joint direction and confirming root joint placement, then moving to count parts before starting the actual implementation file with imports and type definitions.

Writing TypeScript imports and setup...

I'm defining a helper to position and orient rig joints, then starting the build function with the root joint for the treasure hoard scene.

Still writing geometry helpers...

Still building the crown rig...

Working out the arch loop geometry, computing crown points along two perpendicular directions and matching the dome's curve profile to the arch bottom surfaces so they align smoothly.

Now I'm positioning the dome sphere to sit just within the band's inner radius, then shifting to figuring out the ermine brim lathe profile so it doesn't overlap the band's bottom edge, adjusting the y-coordinates to properly stack the brim beneath the band.

Shifting everything up by 0.03, I'm recalculating the arch, dome, orb, and cross positions so they stay symmetric and properly nested -- checking the dome's top clears the arch peak, then placing the orb and cross segments at their new heights.

Now for the fleur decorations positioned around the crown at 45-degree intervals, I'm figuring out cone geometry for the central spike and two leaning side petals, computing tangent-based lean directions so each petal angles outward naturally from its base point.

Moving on to the lion rig, I'm setting up its root bone at the correct position, then starting on the chest panel builder that places box geometry pieces at defined offsets.

For the lid, I'm writing a helper function that creates panel segments between two points, computing length and orientation so each box aligns along the correct direction with proper thickness.

I'm checking that the aim direction stays close to world -X after the lid's rotation, with the thickness axis staying normal in the yz plane, then laying out the lid panels along the outline with centers offset so panels sit centered on the path with proper clearance from the red block beneath.

I'm tracing out the back vertical, slope, top, front slope, and front vertical segments of the lid profile, checking box lengths and corner overlaps, and confirming the width matches between the end caps.

Now I'm verifying that the red block's outline aligns with the panel inner surfaces, checking the top and slope corner offsets for fit, then moving on to work out the gold end cap outline coordinates.

I'm trying to figure out whether the end cap needs a layered design—blue block extrusion with a gold border extrusion around it to match the reference image's lid end detail—and considering how the outline sizes would need to differ for the gold border to actually show.

Skipping lid fleur details for now, I'm placing a gold star-shaped top plate with a sapphire gem centered toward the rear, then adding cone spikes at the chest's top corner posts.

For rivets, I'm scattering small gold spheres along the front and bottom rim edges plus the lid bands, grouping them as merged parts with a flat gold color. I'm also planning separate rivet groups for the lid itself, and sketching sparkle planes near the big ruby that face forward along the z-axis.

Now I'm placing sparkle stars at the crown, sapphire, emerald, goblet rim, and floor gem locations with varying sizes and a glow strength of 1. Then I'm starting the coin builder function, defining a small cylinder geometry and a helper that positions and rotates each coin instance using a transform matrix before pushing it into the geometry list.

Writing coin and merging logic...

I'm skipping the normal-aligned tilt for mound coins since it's a minor detail, and setting up a random number generator for coin placement loops. I'm defining exclusion zones around the crown, main goblet, and fallen goblet so coins don't overlap those objects, while making sure to leave room for the gem.

Still writing the quilt shading function...

I'll skip extra details like buttons and tassels, and move to a helper that converts coordinate arrays into outline points, typed to allow either plain [x,y] pairs or ones marked "sharp".

Now I'm defining an extrude helper that takes a rig, outline, color, position, axis directions, thickness, and optional bevel, calling the extrude function with the appropriate transform. I want bevel only passed when nonzero, and I'm checking that the extrude options support bone attachment and vector directions. For the gem star shape, I'm working out an 8-point outline alternating between outer and inner radii at 45-degree increments, then placing it on the lid's top surface.

I'm recalculating the vertical positioning since the panel is centered at 0.2 with a thickness of 0.03, meaning the outer top surface actually sits at 0.215 rather than my earlier estimate — so I need to shift the band and star/gem outlines upward (around 0.225 for the band top, 0.222 for the star, 0.232 for the gem) to avoid overlap, and I'm adjusting the band outline coordinates to match this new slope. Now I'm moving on to writing the body detail code, starting with the front fleur texture placement.

Setting up the standing and fallen goblet rigs with aim/roll orientation, then building the goblet geometry itself — the lathe body, rim torus, and gem decorations — with the rim torus rotated horizontal around the local y=0.25 position.

Now I'm building the pearl strand chain using a Catmull-Rom spline through sample points, placing 22 pearls evenly along the curve.

Still positioning the pearls and checking placement against the chest rim, then moving to coin stacks and skipping gold bars for now. I'm finalizing the mound's color with a mottled gold texture and preparing to write out all the part definitions before setting up the lid rig.

Setting up the lid's hinge joint and rivet placements along the band tops, converting coordinates into lid rig space, then moving on to the body's gold rope details and sampling coin counts for the hidden mound.

Still scattering coins...

Adding floor rejection logic, varied height and tilt per coin, capping outer ring at 110 accepted after 400 attempts, then 120 chest mound coins plus stacks and gem lists. I'm double-checking the texture function signatures and paint callback types all match correctly before writing the final file with a League of Legends style theme.
